Regarding the draft law on data and data governance, developed in the context of the provisions of the National Programme for the Accession of the Republic of Moldova to the European Union 2025–2029 (Annex A, Cluster 3 – Competitiveness and inclusive growth, Chapter no. 10 – information Society and media). The draft law aims to establish a normative framework for data governance, in order to ensure fair, transparent and secure access to data and to promote its responsible use for the benefit of innovation, economic development and the public interest.

In this context, a revision of the phrasing was recommended, as it was unclear and open to interpretation, failing to clarify whether it referred to personal data or other data categories, with indications of inconsistency towards the European act to be transposed.

In this context, it was considered appropriate to reflect in the draft the essential elements provided for by Regulation (EU) 2022/868, namely, the establishment of a standardized consent form for data altruism and the creation of a Public Register of recognized data altruism organizations, to ensure transparency and public trust.

Finally, it was mentioned that the implementation of data governance mechanisms will require the substantial strengthening of institutional capacities of the competent authorities, particularly in terms of resources, technical expertise and operational capabilities.

Additionally, it was emphasized that the use of personal data in the public interest may involve large-scale processing, including of special categories of data or data concerning vulnerable persons, which generates high risks. In such cases, controllers must perform data protection impact assessments (DPIAs), with the involvement of Data Protection Officers (DPOs) and it was recommended, where possible, to publish their results to increase transparency.

Regarding the obligation to notify the NCPDP in case of requests for personal data, it was mentioned that this is insufficiently clarified, as the purpose and effects of this notification are not specified and the authority does not possess competencies to authorize processing operations. In this context, the necessity to respect the legal mandates of the data protection authority within future data governance mechanisms was underlined.
